guard: connector-owned prefix and model refusals retain distinct allow-listed public codes and persisted scrubbed fatal lines, while stale RuntimeInfo.model cannot override a requested model whose active provider route is verified
why: Issue #985 reproduced a prefixed model reaching the managed session and dying before set_model,
while the host rendered only `startup failed (unknown)` and left no connector log.
The host smoke drives that boundary plus the SDK set_model rejection through real child
processes. It also reproduces measured RuntimeInfo.model lag after successful setModel: the
session journal and active provider route carry the requested pin while the advisory model field
still reports the old default. Mutations reintroduce the obsolete equality gate independently for
model+variant and model-only launches, so both compatibility contracts have a named red.
Persistence is covered twice on purpose. Removing the ONE shared write in startup-diagnostics.ts
stops every diagnostic being persisted, so the suite's first connector-log cell is its honest
first red; naming the later fatal cell there would be a red the mutation never reaches.
Dropping only the fatal line's persistence, while leaving its stderr copy, is what proves the
narrower claim that the scrubbed fatal is written to the seat's own log.

mutations.name: prefixed models collapse back to the unknown startup code
mutations.find:
"model_prefix_rejected",
          `jcode connector: model ${JSON.stringify(config.model)} carries a provider prefix, but the Harness API expects a bare model id — pass ${JSON.stringify(spec.bare)} (the ${JSON.stringify(spec.prefix)} provider is selected by configuration, not by the model id)`,
mutations.replace:
"unknown",
          `jcode connector: model ${JSON.stringify(config.model)} carries a provider prefix, but the Harness API expects a bare model id — pass ${JSON.stringify(spec.bare)} (the ${JSON.stringify(spec.prefix)} provider is selected by configuration, not by the model id)`,

mutations.name: Harness model rejections collapse back to the unknown startup code
mutations.find: throw new JcodeConnectorError("model_refused", "Jcode refused the requested model", { cause: error });
mutations.replace: throw new JcodeConnectorError("unknown" as never, "Jcode refused the requested model", { cause: error });

mutations.name: model and variant startup trusts stale RuntimeInfo.model over the requested active route
mutations.find:
const effectiveModel = config.model ?? runtime?.model;
    const route = effectiveModel ? activeModelRoute(runtime, effectiveModel) : undefined;
mutations.expectRed: model and variant launch succeeds when RuntimeInfo.model lags but the requested active route is verified

mutations.name: model-only startup trusts stale RuntimeInfo.model over the requested active route
mutations.find:
const effectiveModel = config.model ?? runtime?.model;
    const route = effectiveModel ? activeModelRoute(runtime, effectiveModel) : undefined;
mutations.expectRed: model-only launch succeeds when RuntimeInfo.model lags but the requested active route is verified

mutations.name: all connector diagnostics stop being persisted per seat
mutations.expectRed: a successful join with no spawn --prompt names that outcome

mutations.name: the startup fatal line reaches stderr but is no longer persisted per seat
mutations.find: writeJcodeDiagnostic(`[cotal-jcode] fatal: Jcode host startup failed (${startupFailureCode(error)}); inspect the private Jcode logs.\n`);
mutations.replace: process.stderr.write(`[cotal-jcode] fatal: Jcode host startup failed (${startupFailureCode(error)}); inspect the private Jcode logs.\n`);
mutations.expectRed: model_prefix_rejected fatal is persisted in the seat connector log
